items.title: 67520_George Handy oral history interview
items.q: I was fortunate in knowing Gene Orloff who plays violin beautifully, who plays trumpet beautifully, so although he was the originally conceived violinist for the date

ctx.x: Well, I was telling you how the second album came about. Through the first album, which originally was supposed to be someone else's--his name escapes me--the guy that backed out--and as a result of my taking over the first album, they offered me a second one; write anything you want. I said, well, I want to do some experimental work; is that all right with you, creating some new jazz forms, and they said go ahead.

So I conceived of an orchestra of one each, only in the sense that I had one violin, each with a chair, one flute, one trumpet, one trombone, one alto, one tenor, one baritone, bass, piano, drum. I was fortunate in knowing Gene Orloff who plays violin beautifully, who plays trumpet beautifully, so although he was the originally conceived violinist for the date, I
also had the use of his trumpet, which gave me three brass where I wanted it. I just took him off the violin.
